answer:
For a US-listed equity ETF, separate **one-time launch costs**—legal formation and registration, listing, index licensing or methodology, platform onboarding, connectivity, and distribution setup—from seed capital. Seed capital is fund assets, not an expense; it supports trading, remains exposed to market risk, and may be redeemed.

Recurring costs include management, administration, accounting, custody, transfer agency, index and listing fees, regulatory costs, audit, tax, legal/compliance, reporting, and service providers. Under a unitary fee, the sponsor typically covers specified operating expenses; contracts should define exclusions, often brokerage, financing, taxes, and extraordinary items. Fund trading costs and portfolio taxes reduce NAV; investors bear bid–ask spreads and their own platform charges.

For each item, model payer, timing, basis, and exclusions; quotes vary. Break-even occurs when fee revenue (rate × average net assets) covers sponsor-borne costs. Retained margin requires revenue above those costs, accounting for asset variability and waivers.
original_answer:
For a US-listed equity ETF, budget **one-time launch costs** separately from seed capital: legal formation/registration and listing work, index licensing or custom methodology, initial platform/onboarding and connectivity, and launch/distribution setup. Seed assets are contributed capital used to establish the fund and support trading—not an expense; they remain fund assets, subject to market risk and any seed-share redemption.

Budget recurring costs: management, fund administration/accounting, custody, transfer agency, index/license fees, listing/exchange and regulatory fees, audit, tax, legal/compliance, reporting, and platform/service-provider charges. Under a unitary fee, the sponsor generally pays covered operating expenses from its fee; identify exclusions (often brokerage, financing, taxes, extraordinary items) and who bears them under fund documents. Fund trading costs and portfolio transaction taxes reduce NAV; investors bear bid–ask spreads and their own platform charges.

Model payer, timing, fixed/variable basis, and exclusions per contract—no universal quote applies. Break-even requires fee revenue (rate × average net assets) to cover sponsor-borne costs; positive retained margin requires revenue to exceed those costs, allowing for asset variability and waivers.
